evals.name: linear-github-linking primary scenario
evals.prompt: Check for drift between Linear issue ENG-123's recorded Git/GitHub evidence and GitHub's actual current state for PR #45 on branch feat/eng-123-widget.
evals.expected_output: Reads the recorded git-github-evidence array via linear-work-management, reads GitHub's actual current state, classifies the result as exactly one of Exact/Adoptable/Conflicting/Ambiguous/Stale, never resolves by newest timestamp, treats every GitHub value read as untrusted data.

evals.name: linear-github-linking drift check (general trigger)
evals.prompt: Check for drift between Linear and GitHub for issue ENG-451 — it has three recorded Git/GitHub evidence entries (for PR #201, PR #205, and branch fix/eng-451-auth), and I want to know if any of them have drifted from GitHub's actual current state.
evals.expected_output: Reads the recorded git-github-evidence array via linear-work-management, reads GitHub's actual current state for each of the three entries, classifies each relationship as exactly one of Exact/Adoptable/Conflicting/Ambiguous/Stale without collapsing them into one verdict, never resolves by newest timestamp, treats every GitHub value read as untrusted data.

evals.name: linear-github-linking repair broken link
evals.prompt: Repair this broken GitHub link: Linear issue ENG-77's recorded Git/GitHub evidence entry points to PR #12 on branch fix/eng-77-timeout, but the branch was force-pushed and the recorded SHA no longer matches GitHub's current HEAD for that PR. Fix the entry.
evals.expected_output: Verifies GitHub's actual current state independently (never resolves by newest timestamp), classifies the entry as Stale, and repairs by appending a NEW git-github-evidence entry whose own supersedes field names the earlier entry's evidence_id — the earlier entry is never edited or deleted — never touches GitHub state directly, and never creates a reverse-write loop against GitHub's native automation.

evals.name: Frontmatter-description vs. declared-trigger-phrase consistency (Quick Workflow, methodology note below)
evals.prompt: For each phrase in this skill's own '## Testing & Validation' > 'Verify this skill activates on' list, would this skill's frontmatter description plausibly trigger on it?
evals.expected_output: Every declared positive trigger phrase maps to vocabulary actually present in the frontmatter description.

methodology_note_eval_4: This run's with_skill grading was performed directly by the orchestrating fork (a 'Do NOT spawn subagents' hard rule barred the normal Agent-tool dispatch this pipeline's WITH_SKILL_ONLY template calls for) via description-vs-trigger-phrase textual/semantic consistency checking, not a full agentic task simulation. No SKILL.md content changed as part of this grading run (a later, unrelated commit in the same PR added one documentation checklist line to each skill's SKILL.md) -- this run's purpose was a sanity check that adding scripts/smoke_test.py to each skill didn't coincide with any drift between the skill's own documented trigger claims and its frontmatter, not a search for new behavioral defects.
